<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917334_theRebbe_880" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917334_theRebbe_880__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Based on the above, the explanation of the maamar that Moshe is the faithful shepherd who nourishes faith also applies to the shepherds of Israel in every generation, who strengthen Israel's faith to stand with self-sacrifice in fulfilling Torah and mitzvos.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, we can explain what is said in the maamar, that this [aspect] that Moshe is the Raaya Mehemna (the faithful shepherd)</t>
    <t s="1">(who nourishes and sustains faith)</t>
    <t s="2">also applies regarding the shepherds of Israel in every generation</t>
    <t s="3">(the extension of Moshe in every generation)</t>
    <t s="4">who strengthen the faith of Israel so that they stand with self-sacrifice in the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="5">For at first glance,</t>
    <t s="6">this [aspect] that Moshe nourishes and sustains faith is</t>
    <t s="7">(as explained in many places34</t>
    <t s="8">and also in this maamar itself35)</t>
    <t s="9">by means of his bestowing upon Israel knowledge of G-dliness, through which faith comes internally,</t>
    <t s="10">and this [aspect] that the shepherds of Israel in every generation strengthen faith</t>
    <t s="11">(as explained in this maamar36)</t>
    <t s="12">is that the faith of Israel should be in a manner of self-sacrifice.</t>
    <t s="13">And based on the above, we can say,</t>
    <t s="14">that the essential concept of Raaya Mehemna is that he nourishes and sustains faith itself,</t>
    <t s="15">so that faith is not only as it is from the perspective of revelations</t>
    <t s="16">(from the perspective that the soul above sees G-dliness)</t>
    <t s="17">but rather from the perspective of the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="18">And this [aspect] that Moshe draws down faith internally</t>
    <t s="19">(in intellect and comprehension)</t>
    <t s="20">is a result of the fact that he nourishes and sustains faith itself</t>
    <t s="21">(the drawing down and revelation of faith as it is from the perspective of the essence of the soul).</t>
    <t s="22">And as above</t>
    <t s="23">(section 5),</t>
    <t s="24">that the drawing down of faith internally</t>
    <t s="25">(in intellect)</t>
    <t s="26">is through the revelation of the essential bond of the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="27">And based on this, we can say,</t>
    <t s="28">that in this [matter], that in the generations that required actual self-sacrifice, the shepherds of Israel</t>
    <t s="29">(the extension of Moshe)</t>
    <t s="30">strengthened the faith of Israel so that it would be with self-sacrifice,</t>
    <t s="31">the concept of Raaya Mehemna was revealed</t>
    <t s="32">(in this aspect37)</t>
    <t s="33">even more than in Moshe himself.</t>
    <t s="34">For the drawing down and revelation of faith as it is from the perspective of the essence of the soul</t>
    <t s="35">[which is through Moshe and his extension in every generation],</t>
    <t s="36">its primary revelation is through actual self-sacrifice.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The actual self-sacrifice of all Israel for Torah and mitzvos occurred in Purim, and the maamar cites the Midrash that Mordechai was equivalent to Moshe in his generation, revealing the aspect of Raaya Mehemna through revealing the power of self-sacrifice.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, it is known that the actual self-sacrifice for Torah and mitzvos of all Israel was in Purim</t>
    <t s="2">(at the time of Haman's decree).</t>
    <t s="3">For the self-sacrifice of Chanukah</t>
    <t s="4">(at the time of the Greek decree)</t>
    <t s="5">was</t>
    <t s="6">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="7">by Matisyahu and his sons,</t>
    <t s="8">while the self-sacrifice at the time of Haman's decree was by all Israel.</t>
    <t s="9">And based on this, we can explain what is brought in the maamar38</t>
    <t s="10">from the Midrash16</t>
    <t s="11">that Mordechai was equivalent in his generation to Moshe in his generation,</t>
    <t s="12">for although the extension of Moshe is in every generation, nevertheless the Midrash states that Mordechai</t>
    <t s="13">(specifically)</t>
    <t s="14">was equivalent in his generation to Moshe in his generation.</t>
    <t s="15">And we can say,</t>
    <t s="16">that from the virtues of Mordechai the Jew is that he was the Raaya Mehemna</t>
    <t s="17">(in revelation)</t>
    <t s="18">of all Israel in his generation.</t>
    <t s="19">In the manner of Moshe, the Raaya Mehemna, who drew down knowledge to all Israel in his generation,</t>
    <t s="20">as is also understood from the fact that the generation of Moshe</t>
    <t s="21">(all the people of his generation)</t>
    <t s="22">is called the generation of knowledge39.</t>
    <t s="23">[Except that in Moshe, the revelation of this concept</t>
    <t s="24">(that he is the Raaya Mehemna of all Israel)</t>
    <t s="25">was by his drawing down knowledge to all the people of his generation,</t>
    <t s="26">while in Mordechai, the revelation of this concept was by his revealing the power of self-sacrifice that is in all the people of his generation].</t>
    <t s="27">And we can say,</t>
    <t s="28">that by bringing in the maamar the statement of the Midrash that Mordechai in his generation was equivalent to Moshe in his generation,</t>
    <t s="29">through this the author of the maamar ruled a halachic ruling upon himself40,</t>
    <t s="30">that he is the Raaya Mehemna</t>
    <t s="31">(in revelation)</t>
    <t s="32">of all the people of the generation.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The maamar explains the connection and order of topics in the verse "And you shall command," first that Moshe connects Israel to the Ein Sof by nourishing faith, then that the shepherds of Israel in every generation strengthen faith, and finally that the revelation of the "light" (the essence of the soul) is primarily through the extension of Moshe in exile who aroused the power of self-sacrifice.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, we can explain the connection</t>
    <t s="2">(and order)</t>
    <t s="3">of the concepts</t>
    <t s="4">(in the maamar)</t>
    <t s="5">in the explanation of the verse "And you shall command etc.,"</t>
    <t s="6">that at first it explains the interpretation of "And you shall command the children of Israel,"</t>
    <t s="7">that Moshe connects and binds the children of Israel</t>
    <t s="8">(with the Ein Sof)</t>
    <t s="9">by his nourishing and sustaining faith,</t>
    <t s="10">and afterwards it explains that also the shepherds of Israel in every generation</t>
    <t s="11">(the extension of Moshe)</t>
    <t s="12">strengthen the faith of Israel, like Mordechai</t>
    <t s="13">(the Moshe of his generation)</t>
    <t s="14">who strengthened the faith of Israel to stand strong in the study of Torah and fulfillment of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="15">and afterwards it explains the interpretation of "crushed for light"</t>
    <t s="16">(which in the verse "And you shall command" apparently speaks of Moshe himself),</t>
    <t s="17">for this [aspect] that Moshe reveals the quality of the light of Israel</t>
    <t s="18">(the essence of the soul),</t>
    <t s="19">is primarily through his extension in the time of exile</t>
    <t s="20">(crushed)</t>
    <t s="21">who aroused in Israel the power of their self-sacrifice,</t>
    <t s="22">through which is the primary revelation of the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="23">light.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
